arxiv-2301-12538.title: On Approximating the Dynamic Response of Synchronous Generators via Operator Learning: A Step Towards Building Deep Operator-based Power Grid Simulators
arxiv-2301-12538.creator: Christian Moya, Guang Lin, Tianqiao Zhao, Meng Yue
arxiv-2301-12538.description: Abstract This paper designs an Operator Learning framework to approximate the dynamic response of synchronous generators. One can use such a framework to (i) design a neural-based generator model that can interact with a numerical simulator of the rest of the power grid or (ii) shadow the generator’s transient response.

arxiv-2307-00360.title: BatGPT : A Bidirectional Autoregressive Talker from Generative Pre-trained Transformer
arxiv-2307-00360.creator: Zuchao Li, Shitou Zhang, Hai Zhao, Yifei Yang, Dongjie Yang
arxiv-2307-00360.description: Abstract BatGPT is a large-scale language model designed and trained jointly by Wuhan University and Shanghai Jiao Tong University. It is capable of generating highly natural and fluent text in response to various types of input, including text prompts, images, and audio.

arxiv-2412-12634.title: Replications, Revisions, and Reanalyses: Managing Variance Theories in Software Engineering Thanks: Manuscript received December 2024
arxiv-2412-12634.creator: 1 st Julian Frattini, 3 rd Davide Fucci, 4 th Michael Unterkalmsteiner 5 th Daniel Mendez*, 2 nd Jannik Fischbach
arxiv-2412-12634.description: Abstract Variance theories quantify the variance that one or more independent variables cause in a dependent variable. In software engineering (SE), variance theories are used to quantify—among others—the impact of tools, techniques, and other treatments on software development outcomes. To acquire variance theories, evidence from individual empirical studies needs to be synthesized to more generally valid conclusions.

pmc-10616934.title: Assessment of Well-Being Across Menstrual Phases in Female Students
pmc-10616934.creator: Hiroe Washio
pmc-10616934.description: Purpose:In this study, we determined female nursing students' physical and mental state involvement by measuring heart rate variability and salivary α-amylase activity (αAMY).Methods:The study included 108 students aged 20–21 with regular menstrual cycles. The basal body temperature method was used to determine the menstrual phases.

pmc-11433648.title: Heineke-Mikulicz Principle in a Male With Failed Recurrent Urethral Diverticulum
pmc-11433648.creator: Saravanan Jambunathan, Balaji Subramaniam
pmc-11433648.description: Urethral diverticulum with a calculus in a male patient is an uncommon phenomenon, in which the management plan differs from one case to another. The formation of calculi can be attributed to the long-standing urinary stasis in the diverticulum leading to recurrent urinary tract infection and stone formation.

pmc-12594939.title: BRADS and BRWDS: Multipurpose audio and text datasets for automatic Bangla regional speech recognition
pmc-12594939.creator: Umme Aiman, Md Nakibul Islam, MD Hana Sultan Chowdhury, Md. Sadekur Rahman, Md. Tarek Habib, Mahady Hasan
pmc-12594939.description: This paper presents an innovative approach to Bangla voice recognition. Although Bangla is the seventh most spoken native language globally, it remains underrepresented in voice recognition research. The dataset contains 298 frequently used Bangla words, including 233 regional words and 65 standard Bangla words.

pmc-12607181.title: Genome-wide screen uncovers novel host factors for L-A virus maintenance and a potential mutualistic-symbiosis relationship in yeast
pmc-12607181.creator: Wan-Yi Hsiao, Chung-Shu Yeh, Hsin-I Liu, Luh Tung, Tien-Hsien Chang
pmc-12607181.description: BackgroundViruses are traditionally viewed as intracellular parasites that exploit host resources to propagate, often at the host’s expense. However, emerging evidence suggests more nuanced interactions, including potential mutualism. The L-A double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) virus, a non-lytic, cytoplasmic virus commonly found in Saccharomyces cerevisiae, presents an intriguing case, as it lacks clear pathogenic effects in the absence of its M1 satellite.

pmc-12684571.title: Blood Pressure Postural Changes Variability Is Associated With Lower Cognition: The S.AGES Cohort
pmc-12684571.creator: Mathilde Strumia, Jean‐Sébastien Vidal, Philippe Cestac, Brigitte Sallerin, Sandrine Andrieu, Olivier Hanon, Laure Rouch, for the S.AGES investigators
pmc-12684571.description: BackgroundOver the past decade, higher blood pressure (BP) variability and postural changes in BP have been associated with lower cognitive function. However, only one study has investigated the specific association between BP postural changes variability and brain health, showing a greater risk of dementia with higher systolic BP (SBP) postural changes variability.

pmc-13247795.title: Strengths-based resilience: the biopsychosocial factors that differentiate 12-year mental well-being trajectories following adverse childhood experiences
pmc-13247795.creator: Elizabeth Connon, Haeme R.P. Park, Robin M. Turner, Leanne M. Williams, Justine Megan Gatt
pmc-13247795.description: BackgroundAdverse childhood experiences (ACEs) are associated with increased long-term mental and physical health risk, yet inter-individual variation indicates that resilience is possible. Distinct trajectories of sustained mental well-being have been observed among individuals exposed to ACEs, predicting favorable long-term outcomes. However, the biopsychosocial markers underpinning sustained trajectories of resilience remain poorly understood.

pmc-13258337.title: Design of a Recessed Honeycomb Structure with a Nested Star Configuration and Study of Its Static Mechanical Properties
pmc-13258337.creator: Xinlin Wang, Guiwei Liu, Lei Lei, Weihang Peng
pmc-13258337.description: Negative Poisson’s ratio materials show great potential in aerospace, automotive engineering, and military protection owing to their unique deformation behavior and superior mechanical properties. Nevertheless, current negative Poisson’s ratio honeycomb structures suffer from an inherent conflict between stiffness and energy absorption, along with poorly understood mechanical regulation mechanisms in complex three-dimensional nested configurations.

pmc-13302171.title: Incidence and clinical course of pacing-induced cardiomyopathy, predictive role of biomarkers of myocardial damage
pmc-13302171.creator: A Lizancos Castro, A Sarrias, V Bazan, R Villuendas, J Aranyo, F Bisbal, A Bayes Genis
pmc-13302171.description: Background/IntroductionPacing-induced cardiomyopathy (PICM) causes left ventricular dysfunction and heart failure, but its biological mechanisms remain unclear.PurposeTo determine the incidence and clinical course of PICM in patients with preserved LV ejection fraction (LVEF) undergoing dual-chamber pacemaker implantation with expected high RV pacing burden, and to assess the predictive role of selected biomarkers of myocardial damage.

pmc-13383734.title: Modernizing Pesticide Risk Assessment: Technical Advancements as the Path toward Global Food Security
pmc-13383734.creator: Heidi B. Irrig, David J. Miller
pmc-13383734.description: This paper examines how U.S. pesticide science and regulatory frameworks contribute to global food security. It details the use of USDA and FDA monitoring data alongside modernized dietary models (FDD/FCID) to improve the transparency, reproducibility, and potential accuracy of risk assessments.

pmc-13387819.title: The blanking interval after atrial fibrillation ablation: time for reassessment with pulsed field energy—Authors’ reply
pmc-13387819.creator: Juan F Rodriguez-Riascos, Hema S Vemulapalli, James Y Kim, Luis R Scott, Arturo M Valverde, Mayank Sardana, Abhishek J Deshmukh, Suraj Kapa, Chris McLeod, Komandoor Srivathsan
pmc-13387819.description: sed field ablation (PFA) continues to evolve across diverse patient populations, procedural approaches, and management strategies. However, we wish to clarify a central point: our study does not advocate abandoning the blanking period, nor does it suggest that every early recurrence warrants prompt re-ablation.
